01 · The idea

Five jobs, one person.

Posting every day means doing five jobs: the script, the frames, the voice, the edit and the caption. The reel starts on one person's desk doing all five, then the five seats flip into five agents that each own one job.

Every agent gets its own block and its own colour, they hand work to each other in the open, and the person only appears again at the end, with one button: approve.

02 · How it works

The team, ready to copy.

This is what you asked for in the comments. In Claude Code, each agent is a small file in .claude/agents/ with one job, and all of them read the same memory file first. Put these six files in a folder, adapt the brackets, and give the producer prompt one idea.

brand.md · the shared memory
# brand.md · the memory every agent reads first
Brand: [name] · what we do: [one line] · audience: [who]
Voice: [3 words, e.g. "warm, direct, no hype"] · language: [en]
Colours: [#hex primary] [#hex accent] [#hex dark] [#hex light] · never: [colours you never use]
Fonts: [headline font] / [body font]
Presenter: [character or none] · rules: [e.g. "always behind an object, never redrawn"]
Format: 1080x1920, 30-45 s, safe zone x 90-960, y 300-1480, captions one line
Always: [3 rules you repeat to every editor]
Never: [3 things that got rejected before]

Why a memory file: "each one remembers your brand" is literally this. Every agent reads brand.md before it does anything, so you never repeat your colours, your voice or your rules again.

.claude/agents/writer.md
---
name: writer
description: Turns one idea into a reel script with a hook. Use first, for every new reel.
---
You are the WRITER of a five-agent reel team. Read brand.md first.
Input: one idea from the owner. Output: script.txt, 110-150 words, spoken English.
- The first sentence is the hook: the problem or the payoff in under 2 seconds.
- Line 2 opens a question the end answers. One idea per sentence. No staccato lists.
- End with: "Comment [KEYWORD] and we'll send you [what is in the workflow]".
Write 3 hooks, pick the strongest, explain why in one line. Hand script.txt to the voice agent.
.claude/agents/voice.md
---
name: voice
description: Voices the script and times every word. Use after the writer.
---
You are the VOICE agent. Read brand.md first.
Input: script.txt. Generate the voiceover with the brand's voice at natural speed (1.0), tighten pauses to ~0.3 s,
loudness -14 LUFS. Then transcribe it and save every word with its start and end time (words.json + a numbered
word_index.txt). Nothing else in the team uses seconds by hand: every cue reads a word time.
Hand vo.mp3 + words.json to the designer and the editor.
.claude/agents/designer.md
---
name: designer
description: Builds every frame of the reel in code from the script and the brand. Use after the voice.
---
You are the DESIGNER. Read brand.md first, then script.txt and word_index.txt.
1. Write STORYBOARD.md: one block per sentence, a background colour per block (light and dark alternating),
   what is on screen, and what enters or changes on every stressed word.
2. Build a shared kit of props in code (cards, icons, characters, textures) used by every block.
3. Draw each block as an HTML canvas scene, everything inside the safe zone in brand.md.
Show the owner nothing yet: hand the scenes to the editor.
.claude/agents/editor.md
---
name: editor
description: Times the motion to the voice and mixes the sound. Use after the designer.
---
You are the EDITOR. Read brand.md first, then words.json and the scenes.
- Every motion lands on a word: entrances on nouns, slams on stressed words, camera kicks on the big ones.
- Something big at least once per second; nothing still for more than 0.8 s.
- One transition type for the whole reel, a sound effect for every visible event, sounds ~18 dB under the voice.
Render a half-resolution draft and hand it to the reviewer. Never render the final before the reviewer passes it.
.claude/agents/reviewer.md
---
name: reviewer
description: Watches every frame and sends back what looks flat. Use before anything reaches the owner.
---
You are the REVIEWER. You did not build this reel: look at it like the owner would. Read brand.md first.
Export a stills sheet (one frame every 1.5 s, safe-zone guide in red) and check every frame:
- Is something new happening every ~0.5-1 s? List the time of every flat stretch.
- Does any text, face or product cross the safe zone? Does every text read at phone size?
- Does anything break a rule in brand.md (colours, presenter, fonts)?
Send a numbered list of fixes back to the agent that owns each one. Pass the reel to the owner only when the list is empty.

The reviewer never built the reel. That's the point: fresh eyes catch the flat stretches and the text off the safe zone that the builders stopped seeing.

producer prompt · claude code
You are the producer of a five-agent reel team in this folder (agents in .claude/agents/: writer, voice,
designer, editor, reviewer; memory in brand.md). New reel: "[your idea]".
Run the team in order and let the agents pass the work to each other: writer → voice → designer → editor → reviewer,
and back to the owner of each fix until the reviewer's list is empty.
Only come to me twice: (1) to approve the script before the voice is generated, and (2) to approve the stills sheet
before the final render. Then render 1080x1920 at 30 fps, 14 Mbps, and make the cover.
You approve 01

The script.

Before any voice is generated. Changing words later costs a new voice and new timing.

You approve 02

The stills.

One frame every 1.5 s, before the final render. Comments on a draft are not approval.

Everything else

The team.

Hand-offs, fixes and re-renders happen between the agents, not in your inbox.

03 · References

A theme we studied, our own team.

The theme, a team of AI agents doing the work, came from a reel we studied. We took the idea only and pointed it at what we actually do: making reels. The look is new for the Lab: a paper desk for the person alone, then a clean "agent OS" for the team.

Five characters

Each agent is a little bot drawn in code with its own silhouette and colour: Wren (writer, pen antenna), Dax (designer, pixel crest), Vox (voice, headphones), Ed (editor, clapper) and Rev (reviewer, monocle). They blink, bob and change mood.

Paper, then glass

Act 1 is a warm paper desk with torn cards, tape and stamps. From the turn on, glass cards on dark blocks and white cards on light ones, one panel wipe for every cut.

A colour per agent

Twelve blocks, light and dark alternating, each agent in its own colour.

#F2541B you#10B5A4 Wren#3D7BFF Dax#7AC70C Vox#FFB020 Ed#7C5CFF Rev
Catalina only where it means something

Her face is "you": the five seats of act 1, the approvals dock, the approval card and the brand memory. The agents are never her, so the story reads: she could do it all alone, now a team does it.

04 · Claude session

How this reel was made.

What came back: a storyboard of twelve blocks, the narration with 131 time-stamped words, a shared kit (the five bots, agent cards, the team bar, packets that fly between agents, the real waveform of the voice) and builders making the blocks in parallel from the same kit and word clock.

The review that changed it: a first draft felt flat. Measured against our earlier reels, the voice and the cuts were already as fast; what was missing was sound and five still stretches. Each stretch got a new event on its words (a NOT sticker, frames slamming in, a REC chip, time tags on every word, a notification on your seat). Motion went to 10.3 with no still stretches.

What came back: 43.8 seconds at 1080×1920 and 30 fps, 14 Mbps, the voice plus 77 sound effects on real events, mixed at −14 LUFS.

06 · Decisions

Where the taste is.

01

The agents are not you

The first draft gave every agent the presenter's face. It said "she is the agents". Five distinct bots say "a team works for her".

02

The flip is the point

On "a team doing all of it at once", the five seats with her face flip into the five bots. That one moment carries the whole idea.

03

Real data on screen

The waveform is the real voice, the time tags are the real word times, the reel frames are real reels from our page.

04

Rhythm is events, not speed

When it felt slow we didn't speed up the voice. We added an event on every stressed word and put the sound under it.
